rationale: No displayed candidate contains the child’s distinctive administrative sequence: a supplementary bilateral trade agreement conditioned on exchange of a presidential proclamation and a foreign instrument of ratification, followed by a short supplemental proclamation announcing the resulting entry-into-force date. C01 and C23 share section 350 authority and language about entering a trade agreement through a duly empowered plenipotentiary, but those are general trade-agreement formulas embedded in much more elaborate GATT implementation machinery. C15 has a relatively compact sequence in which specified treaty conditions are satisfied and an operative legal consequence is proclaimed, but it terminates an earlier proclamation and does not use the child’s exchange-and-entry-into-force mechanism. These similarities do not establish a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: pursuant to section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended and extended ... I entered into a supplementary trade agreement, through my duly empowered Plenipotentiary
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C01: pursuant to the authority vested in the President ... including the said section 350 ... I entered, through my duly empowered plenipotentiary, into a trade agreement
shared_material.explanation: Close language concerning statutory authority and execution through a plenipotentiary, but it is standard trade-agreement formulation and does not supply the child’s core exchange-of-instruments mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the said supplementary agreement to become effective on and after the thirtieth day following the exchange of my proclamation and the instrument of ratification
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C23: Schedule XX ... will become a schedule to the General Agreement ... on June 6, 1951
shared_material.explanation: Both identify when a trade instrument becomes effective, but C23 uses a different GATT-accession mechanism and lacks the proclamation-for-ratification exchange sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: my proclamation and the instrument of ratification ... were duly exchanged ... [the] agreement ... will come into force on October 11, 1952
shared_material.parent_excerpt: C15: the Republic of Haiti became a contracting party ... and ... all the tariff concessions ... entered into force ... do proclaim that the said proclamation ... is hereby terminated
shared_material.explanation: Both recite fulfillment of treaty-related predicates and then proclaim a legal consequence, but C15’s consequence is termination rather than announcement of entry into force, so the parallel is too general.
